title: Getting Started with React: A Modern Guide
body:
# Getting Started with React React has revolutionized how we build user interfaces. In this guide, we'll explore the fundamentals and best practices for building modern React applications. ## Why React? React offers several compelling advantages: - **Component-Based Architecture**: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state - **Virtual DOM**: Efficient updates and rendering - **Rich Ecosystem**: Vast collection of libraries and tools - **Strong Community**: Active community and extensive documentation ## Setting Up Your First Project The easiest way to start is with Vite: ```bash npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react-ts cd my-react-app npm install npm run dev ``` ## Your First Component Here's a simple functional component: ```tsx import { useState } from 'react'; function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return (

Count: {count}

); } export default Counter; ``` ## Key Concepts ### Props Props allow you to pass data to components: ```tsx function Greeting({ name }: { name: string }) { return

Hello, {name}!

; } ``` ### State Management Use `useState` for simple state: ```tsx const [user, setUser] = useState(null); ``` For complex state, consider: - **useReducer**: Built-in reducer pattern - **Context API**: Share state across components - **Zustand/Redux**: External state management ## Best Practices 1. **Keep components small and focused** 2. **Use TypeScript for type safety** 3. **Follow naming conventions** 4. **Optimize with React.memo when needed** 5. **Use custom hooks for reusable logic** ## Useful Resources - [React Documentation](https://react.dev) - [TypeScript Handbook](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/) - [Vite Guide](https://vitejs.dev/guide/) --- *Happy coding! Remember, the best way to learn React is by building projects.*
